title: Suddenly free
setting: A Sunday evening at home. Okaasan has her phone in her hand after messaging Yuki. She turns to Kenji, who is slumped on the sofa, and asks about next weekend.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, raishuu no doyoubi, jikan aiteru?
lines.ja: ケンジ、来週の土曜日、時間空いてる？
lines.kana: けんじ、らいしゅうのどようび、じかんあいてる？
lines.english: Kenji, are you free next Saturday?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii kara. aiteru no? aitenai no?
lines.ja: いいから。空いてるの？空いてないの？
lines.kana: いいから。あいてるの？あいてないの？
lines.english: Never mind that. Are you free or not?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 土曜は、ちょっと予定ある。
lines.kana: どようは、ちょっとよていある。
lines.english: Saturday I've, um, kind of got plans.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.kana: そう。じゃあ、にちようは？

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nichiyou mo muri. getsuyou, shiken aru kara.
lines.ja: 日曜も無理。月曜、試験あるから。
lines.kana: にちようもむり。げつよう、しけんあるから。
lines.english: Sunday's no good either. I've got an exam on Monday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sokka. yuki ga ne, minna ni gohan ogoru tte. yakiniku da tte.
lines.ja: そっか。ユキがね、みんなにご飯おごるって。焼肉だって。
lines.kana: そっか。ゆきがね、みんなにごはんおごるって。やきにくだって。
lines.english: Oh well. Yuki says she's treating us all to dinner. Yakiniku, apparently.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: yakiniku? a, machigaeta. yotei aru no, sono tsugi no doyou datta.
lines.ja: 焼肉？あ、間違えた。予定あるの、その次の土曜だった。
lines.kana: やきにく？あ、まちがえた。よていあるの、そのつぎのどようだった。
lines.english: Yakiniku? Oh, my mistake. My plans are the Saturday after that.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto? sakki, yotei aru tte itta ja nai.
lines.ja: ほんと？さっき、予定あるって言ったじゃない。
lines.kana: ほんと？さっき、よていあるっていったじゃない。
lines.english: Really? You just said you had plans.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: honto honto. doyou wa aiteru aiteru.
lines.ja: ほんとほんと。土曜は空いてる空いてる。
lines.kana: ほんとほんと。どようはあいてるあいてる。
lines.english: Really, really. Saturday I'm free. Totally free.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo ne, yuki wa doyou, tsugou warui n da tte. nichiyou no yoru nara tsugou ii tte.
lines.ja: でもね、ユキは土曜、都合悪いんだって。日曜の夜なら都合いいって。
lines.kana: でもね、ゆきはどよう、つごうわるいんだって。にちようのよるならつごういいって。
lines.english: Thing is, Saturday's no good for Yuki. She says Sunday evening works for her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji wa nichiyou, tsugou warui n desho? getsuyou, shiken aru n da kara.
lines.ja: ケンジは日曜、都合悪いんでしょ？月曜、試験あるんだから。
lines.kana: けんじはにちよう、つごうわるいんでしょ？げつよう、しけんあるんだから。
lines.english: But Sunday's no good for you, is it? You've got an exam on Monday.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: daijoubu. benkyou wa hiru ni yaru. yoru nara jikan aku kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。勉強は昼にやる。夜なら時間空くから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。べんきょうはひるにやる。よるならじかんあくから。
lines.english: It's fine. I'll study during the day. I'll be free by the evening.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, yuki ni, minna tsugou ii tte renraku shitoku ne. a, ato, doyou wa aiteru n da yo ne?
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキに、みんな都合いいって連絡しとくね。あ、あと、土曜は空いてるんだよね？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきに、みんなつごういいってれんらくしとくね。あ、あと、どようはあいてるんだよね？
lines.english: Right, I'll let Yuki know it works for everyone. Oh, and you're free on Saturday, aren't you?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yokatta. kaimono ni iku kara, tetsudatte ne.
lines.ja: よかった。買い物に行くから、手伝ってね。
lines.kana: よかった。かいものにいくから、てつだってね。
lines.english: Good. I'm going shopping, so you can come and help.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: え、やっぱり手伝いじゃん！
lines.kana: え、やっぱりてつだいじゃん！
lines.english: What? So it IS chores after all!

choices.english: Kenji really does have plans on Saturday, so he'll miss Yuki's dinner and stay home to study for his exam.
Yuki can't make Sunday, so the yakiniku dinner moves to Saturday, and Kenji drops his plans to go.
Kenji claims he's busy all weekend, but once he hears Yuki is treating everyone to yakiniku he's suddenly free, and he ends up helping with Saturday's shopping too.

questions.explanation: Kenji suspects a chore (line 2), so he says he has plans on Saturday (line 4) and can't do Sunday because he has an exam on Monday (line 6). When Okaasan mentions that Yuki is treating everyone to yakiniku (line 7), he suddenly says he got the dates mixed up and is free on Saturday after all (lines 8 and 10). Yuki can only do Sunday evening (line 11), and Kenji says he'll be free by then (line 14). Then Okaasan checks that he's free on Saturday and asks him to help with the shopping (lines 15-17), which was what he was afraid of. A is wrong: Kenji takes back his Saturday plans (line 8) and will go to the dinner. B is wrong: it's Saturday that doesn't suit Yuki, not Sunday (line 11), and the dinner is on Sunday evening.

questions.english: Kenji asks you, "nichiyou no hiru, jikan aiteru? shiken no benkyou, tetsudatte hoshii n da kedo." (Are you free on Sunday during the day? I'd like some help studying for my exam.) Say whether you're free, using aiteru, or jikan aku for when you'll come free.
questions.ja: 日曜の昼、時間空いてる？試験の勉強、手伝ってほしいんだけど。
questions.kana: にちようのひる、じかんあいてる？しけんのべんきょう、てつだってほしいんだけど。
questions.romaji: nichiyou no hiru, jikan aiteru? shiken no benkyou, tetsudatte hoshii n da kedo.
questions.answer: Answer with aiteru (I'm free), or say when you'll come free: un, aiteru yo, or jikan aitara renraku suru ne. In casual speech ga drops (jikan aiteru).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, aiteru yo. nanji kara yaru?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、空いてるよ。何時からやる？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm free. What time do you want to start?

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, hiru wa chotto yotei aru n da. jikan aitara renraku suru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、昼はちょっと予定あるんだ。時間空いたら連絡するね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got something on during the day. I'll message you if I get a moment.

questions.explanation: A free slot 'opens up' (aku), so 'are you free?' is jikan aiteru?, as Okaasan asks in line 1, or just aiteru? as in line 3. Kenji answers with aiteru in lines 10 and 16, and in line 14 he uses plain aku for 'come free': yoru nara jikan aku (I'll be free by the evening). Don't use jiyuu (free as in liberty) or tada (free of charge) here. The second model answer uses both halves of the scene's yes/no pair: yotei aru for the part of the day you're busy, and jikan aitara for 'when I get a moment'. Kenji asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Okaasan first asks about Saturday, what does Kenji say?
questions.ja: ケンジは、最初に土曜日のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじは、さいしょにどようびのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa, saisho ni doyoubi no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Saturday I'm kind of holding plans (word for word from 'have plans').
choices.romaji: doyou wa, chotto yotei o motteru.

choices.english: Saturday I've kind of got plans.
Saturday I've kind of got a scheme (a worked-out plan or project).

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'doyou wa, chotto yotei aru.' Plans exist, so they take aru, and casual speech drops ga. Kenji says it again when he backtracks (line 8: yotei aru no, sono tsugi no doyou datta), and Okaasan throws it back at him (line 9: yotei aru tte itta ja nai). A is wrong: motsu is for holding or owning things, and 'yotei o motteru' copies the English word for word. C is wrong: keikaku is a worked-out scheme, like a project or a trip itinerary, so 'keikaku aru' sounds like he's plotting something, not that he's busy.

questions.english: Okaasan passes on a message from Yuki: "nichiyou no yoru nara tsugou ii tte." What is Yuki saying?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、何と言っていましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんといっていましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nan to itte imashita ka?

choices.english: Sunday evening suits her: she can make it then.
She'll be feeling better by Sunday evening.
She'd rather do Sunday evening, but Saturday would work too.

questions.explanation: Line 11: tsugou ii means a time suits someone, so Sunday evening is when Yuki can make it. In line 15 Okaasan uses it again: minna tsugou ii (it works for everyone). B is wrong: tsugou is about your schedule, not how you feel. Feeling better would be choushi ga ii or kibun ga ii, and nobody is ill. C is wrong: in the same line Okaasan says Saturday is tsugou warui for Yuki, so Saturday doesn't work at all.

questions.english: Imagine you're a friend of Yuki's, and her mother invites you along: "nichiyou no yoru, minna de yakiniku ni iku n da kedo, issho ni dou?" (We're all going for yakiniku on Sunday evening. Want to come?) Turn her down politely, using tsugou.
questions.ja: 日曜の夜、みんなで焼肉に行くんだけど、一緒にどう？
questions.kana: にちようのよる、みんなでやきにくにいくんだけど、いっしょにどう？
questions.romaji: nichiyou no yoru, minna de yakiniku ni iku n da kedo, issho ni dou?
questions.answer: Say Sunday evening doesn't suit you: tsugou ga warui. She's older than you, so keep ga and add desu, or soften it by trailing off with tsugou ga warukute.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, nichiyou no yoru wa chotto tsugou ga warui n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、日曜の夜はちょっと都合が悪いんです。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, Sunday evening doesn't really work for me.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, nichiyou wa chotto tsugou ga warukute.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、日曜はちょっと都合が悪くて。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. But Sunday's a bit difficult for me, I'm afraid.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Okaasan says Saturday is tsugou warui for Yuki, and in line 13 she teases Kenji that Sunday is tsugou warui for him. That's the tactful way to say a time doesn't suit you. The English word 'inconvenient' leads to fuben, but fuben is for places and tools (a shop that's a pain to get to), not for a day. taimingu warui means bad timing, an unlucky moment, so you can't use it to say no. Kenji tells his mother nichiyou mo muri (line 6), which is fine within the family, but with a friend's mother chotto tsugou ga warui is the polite choice. Leaving it trailing (warukute...) makes it softer still.

just as I thought; after all
